items.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021
items.q: so when I was with Art Blakey I had a chance to hang out with Monk one night. Monk came down to hang out with Art, so I hung out with Monk and that was a pleasant surprise

ctx.x: Working with singers, you’re going to go from you may be playing the same tune with two different singers but one’s a man and one’s a woman, and you’ve got to know — you’ve got to be flexible, right? You’ve got to play it in A flat instead of E flat?

Right. Oh yeah. Oh that’s it. You’ve definitely got to be flexible. And then you know, but working with singers, it’s a good experience for keyboard players. Because when you’re playing with a band you could be more forceful. But for high singers you’ve got to be sensitive and you’ve really got to listen. So that’s a good experience for you. But I’ll tell you one thing, man, working with Betty Carter, Monk, that was interesting. Because Betty Carter was like a horn player. Because you know she based her singing…
Well actually you mentioned Joe Williams and he helped us get this project started that we’re doing.
